metadataFromPriorUpload.title: How Should We Judge Biotechnology? Bt Cotton, Hornless Cattle and Stakeholders | Year 12 Biology
metadataFromPriorUpload.description:
Full lesson, notes and practice questions: https://hscscience.com.au/subjects/biology/year12/module6/lesson09.sa

A cotton plant that poisons caterpillars and a bull edited so his calves grow no horns: both work, but is that enough? See how to judge a biotechnology with a concrete benefit, a concrete harm or risk, and who gets each. Follow Bt cotton in Australia, from far fewer insecticide sprays to resistance and refuges, then hornless dairy cattle, where later checks found DNA no one intended. Learn what an animal case adds, how to sort objections into consequences, distribution and principle, and how to end an evaluation with a verdict. Two exam-style questions with brief feedback.

0:00 Two biotechnologies that work
0:25 What a judgement needs
0:53 Bt cotton: the benefit, and who gets it
1:30 Bt cotton: the risks, and who carries them
2:08 A verdict with a condition
2:38 The animal case: hornless dairy cattle
3:18 Checking what actually happened
3:53 What an animal case adds
4:13 Three kinds of question
4:38 Memory
4:59 Attempt one (Golden Rice)
5:39 Feedback, item one
6:07 Attempt two (AquAdvantage salmon)
6:43 Feedback, item two
7:11 Decision rule and handoff
7:35 Key notes

Biology 2017: Year 12 Module 6, Genetic Change. Inquiry question: "How do genetic techniques affect Earth's biodiversity?"
Syllabus dotpoint (NSW Biology Stage 6, 2017, Module 6):
"investigate the uses and applications of biotechnology (past, present and future), including: (ACSBL087)
- analysing the social implications and ethical uses of biotechnology, including plant and animal examples
- researching future directions of the use of biotechnology
- evaluating the potential benefits for society of research using genetic technologies
- evaluating the changes to the Earth’s biodiversity due to genetic techniques"
Official 2017 course: https://www.nsw.gov.au/education-and-training/nesa/curriculum/science/biology-stage-6-2017

Prerequisite: What counts as biotechnology? Next: Which future biotechnology uses are plausible?
